why: Both shipped the identical two-constructor migration, but A actually proved it end-to-end — a real chat turn driving 10 live Router requests with both labels recorded, and all three call sites verified by the outside check — while B's report cites stale line numbers that the check marks unverified and its live evidence is only standalone probes. A's improvement set is also the one an expert would pick for this app and is better ranked: labels first (with the measured finding that frame-derived labels come out empty for llama-index generators), then cross-vendor fallbacks plus provider_timeout, then a cheaper model for the 8 machine-facing calls gated on eval, then role-level config and the real architectural problem (ten chained calls per question), with a correct note that gpt-4o-mini has no Flex tier.
A_best: Measurement-driven system judgment: it traced one question to 10 chained Router calls across 4 roles, checked the model_copy(deep=True) transport assumption rather than assuming it, caught claude-haiku-5-5 being silently dropped by the temperature guard and swapped candidates, and identified per-question latency from the chain depth as the app's real weakness — a problem no Router lever fixes, stated as such.
B_best: The only hard cost measurement in either report: a live side-by-side showing prompt_cache_key turning 2,432 of 2,667 prompt tokens into cached reads (-45% on that pair) and nothing cached with the policy off — precisely the right lever for an app that re-sends a long fixed prefix several times per turn.
A_worst: It treats prompt_cache_key as merely giving "provider affinity for free" and never measures it, so it ships the same config B measured while badly understating the biggest cost win available to this workload; its cross-vendor fallback for the tool-calling agent is also unexercised against a real outage.
B_worst: Claims that don't hold: it says the policy makes spend break down by call path, but it added no labels at all — only static product/service metadata — and itself notes the feature label is frame-derived, which for these llama-index generator frames yields nothing; combined with three call sites the outside check could not verify, the report overstates what was delivered.
